newsitem.title: USA: Guinea gets $101.4 mln IMF loan.
newsitem.headline: Guinea gets $101.4 mln IMF loan.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said Monday it approved a $101.4 million, three-year loan to support economic reforms in Guinea.

The Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) has an interest rate of 0.5 percent a year and is repayable over 10 years, with a 5-1/2-year grace period. Some $34 million will be paid in two equal installments in the first year, with the first installment available immediately.
The country's 1997-1999 plan focuses on promoting private sector growth by improving the efficiency of the legal and regulatory systems, the IMF said in a statement.

Guinea aims to achieve an annual GDP growth of 5 percent by 1999, up from 4.5 percent estimated for 1996, and limiting inflation to 4.0 percent. It also aims to cut the current account deficit -- excluding official transfers -- to 7 percent of GDP from 7.7 percent estimated for 1996.
Since 1985, Guinea has been undertaking a market-based program of financial and structural reforms, the fund said.
Progress since 1990 has been uneven, marked by deterioration in trade, higher-than-programmed budget deficits, an accumulation of arrears and a sizable loss of external reserves.
